concepts.preferred_label: Aortic stenosis with preserved left ventricular function
concepts.why: The patient's echocardiogram shows moderate aortic stenosis with preserved biventricular systolic function.
The patient has a history of radiation therapy, which can cause cardiomyopathy, and the echocardiogram shows preserved biventricular systolic function.
The patient's ECG findings demonstrate frequent pauses and premature atrial complexes, which can be associated with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
The patient's symptoms of intermittent confusion and falls, combined with the absence of acute distress, suggest a possible cerebral vasculopathy.
The patient's ECG findings and intracardiac recordings demonstrate conduction abnormalities, which can be associated with cardiac sarcoidosis.
The patient has a history of renal cell carcinoma treated with chemotherapy and radiation, which increases the risk of developing lymphoma.
The patient has a history of renal cell carcinoma, which can metastasize to other parts of the body.
